answers.label: Benefits and challenges of consequential methods
answers.text:
We appreciate the GHG Protocol’s proposal of using consequential assessment to determine the actual emissions impact of electricity related projects and welcome the intent to link these actions more directly with real-world power sector decarbonisation.

We support the introduction of a framework that evaluates whether electricity projects genuinely displace fossil fuel generation and contribute to systemwide emissions reductions.

We agree that the distinction between inventory accounting and real-world impact is important, and we recognise that this additional form of assessment will provide valuable insight into the true emissions consequences of energy projects.

However, we seek further clarification regarding where and how this consequential assessment will be reported. It is not yet clear to us how and where this separate reporting mechanism will sit.

We assume that a dedicated reporting channel or disclosure framework may be developed to capture the fossil fuel displacement impact of such projects. We would welcome further guidance from the GHG Protocol on how such reporting will be structured and how organisations should prepare for these expectations.

Overall, we support the proposed change and believe that it will enable a more complete picture of the real emissions benefits of electricity-sector interventions. We look forward to further detail on how these findings should be disclosed in practice.

audit_basis: An Irish airport operator filed in the Transportation sector; writes as a reporting company ('We support the introduction of a framework...').
